name: Textiles

mofsl_2qfy27.headline: Sector outperforms; strong outlook intact (printed as 'TEXTILE')
mofsl_2qfy27.read: Aggregate coverage revenue grew 19.9% YoY, EBITDA 62.7%, EBITDA margin rose to 15.0% (11.0% in 2QFY26) and adjusted PAT grew 103.1%. Spinning (Vardhman Textile) grew 16% on ~98-100% utilisation and yarn realisations up ~21% YoY to INR327/kg, with the yarn-cotton spread widening to ~INR140/kg from INR111/kg on China and Bangladesh demand; the duty-free cotton import window was extended to Dec'26. Apparel (KPR, Arvind, Pearl Global, Gokaldas) posted revenue/EBITDA/PAT growth of 23%/47%/142%, led by Pearl Global (realisations +~20%, volumes +15%); home textiles revenue rose ~23% with margin up ~530bp to ~15% from 9%, Indo Count stood out (core realisations +19%, volumes +11%) and Welspun margin expanded 565bp. Guidance: apparel and home textile managements kept revenue and margin guidance (Welspun and Indo Count at double-digit growth); spinning margins are expected to normalise in 2HFY27 but stay healthy. MOFSL keeps BUY on GEXP, ARVND, PGIL, ICNT and WELSPUNL and Neutral on KPR, VTEX and TRID.

unit_economics: Spinner: EBITDA = volume x (yarn price/kg - cotton cost/kg - conversion cost/kg), so the yarn-cotton spread is the profit pool. Exporters: revenue = volume x USD realisation x USD/INR, EBITDA = revenue - raw material (cotton, yarn, fabric) - labour, freight and power + export incentives (RoDTEP, RoSCTL).

price_drivers.why: Spread widened to ~INR140/kg from INR111/kg in 2QFY27, lifting aggregate EBITDA margin to 15.0%; MOFSL expects it to normalise in 2HFY27, which is the main earnings risk for spinners.

price_drivers.driver: Export realisation and volume (US, UK/EU demand)
price_drivers.why: Pearl Global realisations rose ~20% with volumes +15% and Indo Count core realisations +19% with volumes +11%; US tariff revisions, the AGOA extension and UK/EU FTAs decide whether order books hold.
Cotton costs are being passed through in home textiles; lagging pass-through or a Cotlook A and Shankar-6 spike compresses exporter gross margin first.
India's tariff competitiveness and buyer diversification away from China drove home textile revenue +~23% and margin +~530bp in the quarter.
Management flags freight and fuel as monitorables and apparel wages as headwinds; margins improved only from a low base.

kpis.name: Yarn-cotton spread (Rs/kg) and realisation
kpis.definition: Cotton yarn selling price per kg less raw cotton cost per kg of yarn (cotton price adjusted for waste), tracked against Indian Shankar-6 and Cotlook A.
kpis.formula: yarn realisation (Rs/kg) - cotton cost (Rs/kg); reported by spinners in decks
kpis.why_it_moves_price: Each Rs10/kg of spread on a 100 million kg spinner is Rs1bn of EBITDA; the widening from INR111/kg to ~INR140/kg and yarn realisation +21% to INR327/kg is why spinning EBITDA surged, and expected normalisation in 2HFY27 sets the earnings peak that the market prices.
kpis.history_source: get_investor_presentation with metric filter 'spread' or 'yarn realisation' for Vardhman Textile (VTL), Welspun and other spinners if indexed; otherwise list_library_documents for company decks and broker results notes (MOFSL textile thematic, Jun 2026, shown on page 41 of the strategy report); get_commodity_prices for cotton if covered.
kpis.estimate_source: No consensus for spreads; get_consensus_estimates gives Sales, EBITDA and EPS for covered names only; MOFSL and other broker models in the library; management spread commentary in transcripts.
kpis.traps: Companies quote yarn and cotton on different weights and quality bases; cotton inventory lags give spot spread vs accounting spread; Cotlook A, Shankar-6 and MCX prices differ; duty-free import windows change landed cost.

kpis.name: Realisation per unit and volume growth by segment
kpis.definition: Revenue per kg or per piece and unit volume growth for home textile (bath linen, bedding, flooring), apparel garments and yarn.
kpis.formula: revenue growth = volume growth x realisation growth; realisation = revenue / units
kpis.unit: % YoY, Rs or USD per unit
kpis.why_it_moves_price: Separates price from demand: Pearl Global realisations +~20% and volumes +15%, Indo Count core realisations +19% and volumes +11% show durable order flow; realisation-only growth reverses when cotton falls.
kpis.history_source: get_investor_presentation filters 'realisation' and 'volume' for ICIL, WELSPUNLIV, PGIL, GOKEX and others if indexed; transcripts via search_research; get_financials for revenue, with units from decks.
kpis.estimate_source: Company revenue guidance in transcripts (home textile and apparel players kept guidance, Indo Count and Welspun at double-digit growth); get_consensus_estimates for Sales and EBITDA; no consensus on volume.
kpis.traps: Realisation includes currency (USD/INR) and mix (flooring, pillows vs sheets); container delays shift shipments across quarters (Indo Count 1Q shipments fulfilled in 2Q); acquisitions.

kpis.name: EBITDA margin
kpis.definition: Operating profit before depreciation over revenue from operations, with export incentives separated where disclosed.
kpis.formula: EBITDA / revenue from operations; ex other income
kpis.why_it_moves_price: Aggregate margin rose to 15.0% from 11.0% a year ago and home textile margin by ~530bp; the market capitalises margin sustainability, so the debate is whether spread and tariff gains persist as spreads normalise.
kpis.history_source: get_financials (revenue, raw material, employee cost, other expenses); get_investor_presentation filter 'EBITDA margin'; MOFSL sector tables for aggregate series.
kpis.estimate_source: get_consensus_estimates for EBITDA and Sales (derive margin); management margin guidance in transcripts (maintained); broker models in the library.
kpis.traps: Export incentives (RoDTEP, RoSCTL) sit in other operating income for some; FX gains in other income; inventory gains in spinning when cotton rises; low-base effect from FY26 margins of 10.6-11.0%.

kpis.name: Capacity utilisation and capex
kpis.definition: Utilisation of spindles, looms and stitching capacity and the capex announced for expansion and modernisation.
kpis.formula: production / installed capacity; capex per unit capacity
kpis.why_it_moves_price: Spinners ran at ~98-100% utilisation in 2Q, so earnings growth must come from spread or new capacity; capacity additions across spinners and integrated players raise supply risk to spreads.
kpis.history_source: get_investor_presentation filters 'utilisation' and 'capacity'; MD&A and annual report extracts in the library; transcripts for capex plans.
kpis.estimate_source: Management capex and expansion guidance in transcripts; broker models; no consensus.
kpis.traps: Utilisation defined on shifts and product mix; announced capacity vs commissioned; spinners' capex includes modernisation.

kpis.name: US revenue share and tariff status
kpis.definition: Share of revenue from the US and the tariff rate applied to Indian textile exports versus competing countries.
kpis.formula: US revenue / total revenue; tariff differential vs Vietnam, Bangladesh, Pakistan, China
kpis.why_it_moves_price: Home textile exporters earn 50-70% of revenue in the US, so a tariff change moves EBITDA directly; the 2Q margin gain came from India's improved tariff position and sourcing diversification, and any US tariff revision is the largest single stock catalyst.
kpis.history_source: get_investor_presentation filters 'US' and 'geography'; transcripts via search_research with 'tariff' query; MOFSL Textile thematic (Jun 2026) in the report library.
kpis.estimate_source: No consensus on tariff scenarios; management commentary in transcripts; broker sector notes in the library.
kpis.traps: Tariff effective dates vs order shipment dates; customers absorbing part of duties; price negotiations leave realisation unchanged for a quarter.

kpis.name: Export incentives (RoDTEP, RoSCTL, duty drawback)
kpis.definition: Government export incentive income as a percentage of export revenue.
kpis.why_it_moves_price: Incentives are 2-5% of export revenue at near-100% margin, so a rate change or scheme lapse can move EBITDA margin by 100-300bp for exporters; the market treats them as policy-dependent.
kpis.history_source: get_financials other operating income; annual report notes in the library via read_library_document; transcripts for scheme rates.
kpis.estimate_source: No consensus; broker models and management commentary on scheme continuity; DGFT notifications referenced in notes.
kpis.traps: Booked in other operating income or net of revenue; catch-up recognition of prior-period claims; rate cut-offs by product category.

kpis.name: USD/INR realised rate and hedge position
kpis.definition: Average realised rate on export receipts and the forward cover, with the EBITDA sensitivity per 1% move.
kpis.formula: reported realised rate; EBITDA sensitivity per 1% INR move
kpis.why_it_moves_price: More than 80% of revenue is USD-linked for home textile exporters against INR cost; each 1% INR depreciation adds roughly 40-60bp to EBITDA margin before hedges, so rate moves change EPS estimates.
kpis.history_source: get_commodity_prices for INR:USD; transcripts for hedge cover; get_financials for FX gains and losses line.
kpis.estimate_source: Bloomberg and broker INR assumptions via get_commodity_prices; company hedge disclosures in transcripts.
kpis.traps: FX gains in other income vs revenue; hedge book rates lag spot by 6-12 months; translation vs transaction effects.

kpis.name: Inventory days and net working capital
kpis.definition: Cotton, yarn and finished goods inventory days and net working capital as days of sales.
kpis.formula: average inventory / COGS x 365; NWC days
kpis.why_it_moves_price: Cotton bought ahead of price moves gives inventory gains or losses that swing spinner margins by 200-400bp, and rising retailer inventory in the US delays orders; cash flow and net debt drive the multiple for leveraged names.
kpis.history_source: get_financials balance sheet inventory, receivables and payables; get_investor_presentation filters 'inventory days' and 'net debt'.
kpis.estimate_source: No consensus; management working-capital and debt guidance in transcripts; broker models in the library.
kpis.traps: Cotton season inventory build in 3Q; letter-of-credit and export bill discounting treated as payables; inventory valuation method.

macro_inputs.series: Cotton prices: Cotlook A (US cents/lb) and Indian Shankar-6 (Rs/candy)
macro_inputs.source: Airavat get_commodity_prices for cotton if covered; otherwise MOFSL textile notes in the library
macro_inputs.why: Raw material cost for spinners and exporters; the duty-free import window to Dec'26 caps domestic prices

macro_inputs.series: Cotton yarn price (Rs/kg) and China and Bangladesh demand
macro_inputs.source: Spinner decks and broker textile notes in the report library
macro_inputs.why: Yarn realisation was ~INR327/kg (+21% YoY) in 2Q; demand abroad set the spread

macro_inputs.series: US tariff rates on Indian textiles; UK/EU FTAs; AGOA extension
macro_inputs.source: Broker sector notes and transcripts via search_research
macro_inputs.why: Demand and pricing power for apparel and home textile exports

macro_inputs.series: US retailer inventory and orders; USD/INR; container freight
macro_inputs.source: Broker notes; Airavat get_commodity_prices for INR:USD
macro_inputs.why: Order flow, realisation and freight cost

valuation_anchor: EV/EBITDA and P/E on mid-cycle margins against own multi-year band; spinners on EV/EBITDA at normalised spread (not peak spread); exporters on P/E with US tariff scenarios.
watch_next_quarter: Per MOFSL, spreads and margins are expected to normalise in 2HFY27 but remain healthy: monitor cotton prices and the duty-free import window ending Dec'26, freight and fuel costs, US and EU demand recovery and tariff changes, and whether home textile and apparel managements hold their revenue and margin guidance.
